text:
Alex: Quick async — can someone run a focused micro-profiling + quality sweep for qcompact-v2 across int8, int4, and fp8 on the hopper-prod pool? Need tail-latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, and eval delta on our webqa-edgecases-v2 promptset. Target seq_len=1024, batch sizes 1 and 8.

Marta: Which eval metric exactly? we track EM/F1 for QA and avg logprob for gen, right? :thinking_face:

Alex: Right — primary is F1 on QA subset + avg generation perplexity on the longform subset. Also want a small per-prompt diff CSV so we can spot regressions.

bench-bot: Job queued: bench-2023456789-01. Estimated 45m. Will post artifacts to s3://redwood/bench/results/2023456789 when done.

Chris: heads-up — earlier int4 runs showed a consistent ~2.2% F1 drop on the summarization subset vs int8. Could be kernel quant scaling or attention head clipping. I'll attach the small repro later.

Sophie: I can kick this off on dedicated hopper. Two notes: 1) pass KV_CACHE_ON=true for long sequences, 2) set BATCH_WINDOW_MS=6 to keep latency tighter. Command I usually run:
```
./tools/run_bench.sh \\n  --model qcompact-v2 \\n  --variants int8,int4,fp8 \\n  --seq 1024 \\n  --batch-sizes 1,8 \\n  --prompts s3://redwood/promptsets/webqa-edgecases-v2 \\n  --save s3://redwood/bench/results/2023456789/results.json \\n  --env KV_CACHE_ON=true,BATCH_WINDOW_MS=6
```

Dan: pinging @Marta and @Chris — I left a small PR with the quant-scaling fix and a unit test (https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/7890). Would love a quick review before we run the sweep.

Marta: I'll take the PR this afternoon PT. If the test passes locally I'm happy to merge before the long run. :+1:

Alex: For the eval harness, please run with seed=42 and n_samples=50 for each variant so diffs are comparable. Also produce token-latency histograms (CSV) and per-batch GPU utilization.

bench-bot: bench-2023456789-01 started on hopper-prod-gpu-07 (gpu:H100). Logs streaming: https://internal.logs/bench/2023456789-01

Chris: If int4 still regresses, try toggling `quant_scale_mode` from `per-channel` to `per-tensor` for attention weights as a quick ablation. I suspect the headwise scaling mismatch.

Sophie: Running now. Will post interim numbers (p50/p95/p99) ~20m after start.

deploy-bot: Reminder: dedicated pool maintenance window 2023-10-12 02:00-03:00 UTC — running long benches across that window may get preempted.

Alex: Good call. Sophie — can you avoid that window? If it starts before completion, cancel and reschedule.

Sophie: Noted — scheduling to finish before 02:00 UTC.

bench-bot: bench-2023456789-01 finished. Artifacts: s3://redwood/bench/results/2023456789/results.json, plots: s3://redwood/bench/results/2023456789/plots.zip

Marta: Quick skim: int8->baseline, fp8 matches int8 on F1 (+0.3%), int4 shows -2.0% on QA F1 and -3.1% on summarization perplexity. Latency: int4 is 1.8x tokens/sec vs int8, p95 latency reduced 28%.

Chris: Can you paste the per-prompt diff for the top 10 worst regressions? want to see if it's localized to specific tokens or longer contexts.

Marta: Dropping CSV snippet:
```
prompt_id,variant,delta_f1,notes
q1234,int4,-8.6,missing named entities at tail
q2345,int4,-6.1,collapsed list generation
q5678,int4,-5.0,formatting truncation
q9012,fp8,+0.4,ok
q3456,int8,-0.2,ok
```

Alex: Thanks — looks like edge long-context entity recall failing under int4. That points to quantization of attention or KV scaling. Chris, if your per-head scaling idea holds, we can toggle in runtime and re-run only the failing subset to save time.

Chris: I'll push a small runtime flag `--quant-scale=per-tensor` to the canary branch and re-run the top 50 failing prompts. PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/7893

Sophie: Can run that micro-run once PR is merged. Ping me when ready and I'll schedule a 10m run.

Dan: Reviewed PR #7890 earlier, left one nits comment. Will follow up on #7893 today.

Alex: Plan: merge quant-scaling PR if tests pass, re-run micro-bench on top 50 prompts for int4 with per-tensor scaling, collect F1 + token-latency. If regression goes away -> consider shipping int4 with that runtime knob for now and open follow-up to audit kernel scaling.

Marta: Sounds good. I'll create a short tracker issue with the artifacts and tag SRE/runtime for visibility.

Sophie: Micro-run scheduled after PR merge. I'll post results in this thread. :rocket:

bench-bot: micro-bench-2023456789-02 queued.

Alex: Thanks team — big win if we can keep int4 perf but avoid the quality hit. If micro-run still regresses we'll fallback int4->int8 for production canary and roll fp8 as candidate.

Marta: Filing issue: https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/4567 — added artifacts and initial notes.

Sophie: micro-bench completed: int4+per-tensor -> F1 delta -0.4% vs int8 (was -2.0%), latency still 1.7x. Uploading CSVs.

Chris: that's promising. I'll open a follow-up to investigate per-head vs per-tensor tradeoffs in kernels and add unit tests for attention quant scales.

Alex: Great progress. Closing loop: @Dan can you coordinate a quick Docs blurb for runtime knobs and an opt-in flag for int4 per-tensor until we harden kernels?

Dan: Yup, will draft in docs/notes and ping for reviews.

Marta: I'll mark this done in the sprint board after PR merges and docs are live. :white_check_mark:

Alex: Thanks all — thread archived when docs + PRs merged. :tada:
